text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- U.S Secretary of State Madeleine Albright arrived in Hanoi on Thursday for an official visit. She is scheduled to witness the signing of a copyright treaty and declaration of the establishment of consulate-generals.
-- Defence Vice Minister and Army Chief of General Staff Lt-General Pham Van Tra began an official visit to Burma on Thursday.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has signed a decision allowing for a continuation of tax exemption on imported materials for foreign investment projects.
-- Vietnam and Turkey expect to sign a trade accord in late August.
-- Finance Minister Nguyen Sinh Hung has said the government will only allocate capital for state enterprises which operate efficiently and profitably.
-- Vietnam has strongly condemned the killings of three Vietnamese nationals in Cambodia and has called on the Cambodian authorities to carry out an investigation into the case.
-- Science, Technology and Environment Minister Pham Gia Khiem says Vietnam wants more effective and closer coordination in environmental management.
-- Hanoi city reported industrial output growth of 12 percent in the first half of 1997.
-- More than $195 million worth of State Treasury bonds have been sold so far this year.
-- Vietnam's Labour Union says the number of drug addicts in the country has reached 185,000. Eighty percent of them are involved in crime.
-- Vietnam will stop issuing licences for tobacco joint-ventures.
